localChanges: When a computer civilization loses its last city, it now comes back as one new civilization. Each unit the lost city had supported was bringing another one back, so a single defeat could add four or five civilizations at once, and a game could run out of civilizations to come back as within a few turns (closes #600).

log: When the city was its player's last, disbanding the first unit defeats the player, which destroys the rest; the loops over the city's supported units then destroyed each of those a second time, running every unit `Destroyed` rule again (civ-clone/web-renderer#600). Both loops now skip a unit that is already destroyed.

Losing its last city disbands the units the city supported, and each of those destroyed units checked whether its player was now defeated: the city had already changed hands, so every one of them processed `Defeated` for the same player, as did the capture itself afterwards, and civ1-game-end's respawn brought a civilization back for each (civ-clone/web-renderer#600). The three rules that defeat a player on losing a unit or a city now check, as their effect runs, that the player is still in the game, with the `PlayerRegistry` passed to them as to the `Defeated` rules. As their effect, not a criterion: a rule set's criteria are all evaluated before any of its effects run, and the disbanding that defeats the player first is an earlier effect of the same set.
